description_en: On the basis of radiocarbon dating, the Dhanaju Caitya Temple, a miniature temple with a caitya in the sanctum, located at the Ituṃ Bāhāḥ Ṭola, was determined to be the earliest extant Temple of the Kathmandu Valley built in the 10th century (cp. Gutschow 2011, p. 219).Locke (1985, p.290) referred to this miniature Temple as Dhavala Caitya Vihāra. However, none of the scholars working on the monasteries of the Valley have classified this as abāhāḥorbahī. Locals also refer to it as ‘aśoka caitya’ rather than ‘bāhāḥ’. The Temple-roof is covered with brass sheets and topped with akalaśa-shaped finial made with copper. The woodentoraṇaplaced atop the sanctum door has been already stolen (only its lower part has survived). Inside the sanctum of the Temple is a stonecaitya. It is also known as ‘dhavala(white/bright)caitya’because it is painted white. An aniconic stone is located north of the Temple, and the locals revere it as Bhakku (Ākāśa Bhairava). To the south of the Temple is adharmadhātujinālaya caitya.It is unknown why thecaityawithin the Temple is referred to as ‘dhanaju’. Probably, someone called Dhanaju built and named it after him as ‘Dhanaju Caitya’. However, there are no historical records of the construction of the Temple andcaitya. In 1894 (NS 1014), the Temple was renovated and atoraṇawas offered. Before it was destroyed by earthquakes in 1934 CE, the Temple had two tiers and a circumambulatory path around it. Thegaḥjhyāḥ(blind window) beneath the roof should have been on the first floor, but it was moved there after the Temple was rebuilt as a single tier following the earthquake. In 1983 CE, thejhĩgaṭīroof was replaced with corrugated metal sheet (Gutschow 2011, p. 220). The Temple was recently renovated in 2021 CE (VS 2077).Gutschow(2011, p.219) describes the Temple as follows: “It contains the fragment of a Licchavicaitya with a recent finial. The temple is a small square structure measuring 182 centimetres along the sides, with thresholds in each direction in stone, frames around the openings, secondary jambs (hāchenbāhāḥ) with colonnettes (toraṇthān) in front, and a double stepped cornice (cvakulān) on top. The small size probably explains whey the conventional primary bearing frame was omitted. On the other hand, corner pillars added richness to the structural design. The wall surfaces were plastered in 1989, whicle three tympana demonstrate an earlier renewal of the temple in 1899 (inscription on the bottom of the tympanum, elevation west). The former so-called hanging roof (yengaḥpākhā) was replaced by a joist roof (dhalinpākhā), its struts supported by the lower cornice. Three of the small niche panels, each carved from a single piece of wood, are fixed between simple, uncarved struts (…). Quite extraordinary is the sequence of ten carved wooden elements (including four cornices) to frame nine larger niches (with the four Tathāgatas in the centre) and 17 smaller niches on each side. The string course between the first and second cornices features lotus motifs in the north and east, ganders (haṃsa) with crossed necks in the south and a pair of gees framing a lotus flower in the west. The Tathāgatas of the central niches follow the accepted order, with Amitābha facing west, Amoghasiddhi north, Akṣobhya east, and Ratnasambhava south. Their lotus throne has a backrest in the archaic style, including a prominent crossbar that supports a pair ofmakarasfacing inwards on the western and northern elevations. On the eastern and southern elevations the aquatic animal is replaced by lotus foliage, but both motif symbolise the abundance of celestial waters. (…) The dating to the 9thor 1th century based on a comparison with the upper decorative panel of the 7th-century frame of Amitābha’s shrine in the eastern wing of the Jokhang in Lhasa (see p. 190) and confirmed by radiocarbon testing. There the framing of five niches with pilasters topped by capitals, the shaping of the wisdom-bearers with fluttering scarves and the flexing of the legs is almost identical. A similar architectural framing is also found at the 7th-century Licchavicaitya G in Cabahil (see p. 201). The Tathāgata’s throne under a canopy resembles that of Kuber at the blind window of Ukubāhā, while the aedicule of Susunani has an architectural frame featuring a pair of makaras in the principal niche and the Tathāgata under a canopy in a secondary miniature niche on top of the aedicule (see p. 248). Never again did such carved wooden panels appear in Newar architecture. The farming of niches with miniature pilasters supporting tympana evolved at 8thcentury Licchavicaityas and on the 9th-century Sasunani and Ukubāhā aedicules. The depiction of heads of divine or human figures emerging from niches with a shouldered frame probably served as prototype for the blind windows, which seem to have first appeared three hundred years later at the Ratneśvara and Viśveśvara temples”.
description_ne: ईशाको १० औं शताब्दीमा निर्माण गरिएको यो मन्दिरको उत्तरमा सवःभक्कु नाचसित सम्बन्धित भक्कु (आकाश भैरव) को आकृतिविहीन ढुङ्गा स्थापना गरिएको छ ।इतुं बाहाः टोलमा रहेको कायग ननिमा पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी एक तले मन्दिरभित्र धनजु चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ । चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको यस मन्दिरलाईLocke(1985, p.290) ले धवल चैत्य विहार भनेका छन् । तर काठमाडौंका बाहाः बहीसम्बन्धी अध्येताहरूले यसलाई बाहाःको सूचीमा राखेका छैनन् । स्थानीयहरू पनि यसलाई बाहाः भन्दैनन् । उनीहरू यसलाई अशोक चैत्य भनी पूजा गर्छन् । यस मन्दिरको छानामा पित्तलको पाता राखिएको छ । छानामाथि तामाको कलशलाई गजूरको रूपमा स्थापना गरिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामाथि राखिएको काष्ठतोरण चोरी भइसकेको छ, तोरणको तल्लो अंश मात्र बाँकी रहेको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र ढुङ्गाको अशोक चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ । चैत्यको गर्भमा सेतो रङ्ग लगाइएकोले यसलाई धवल चैत्य पनि भनिन्छ । मन्दिरको उत्तरमा आकृतिविहीन ढुङ्गा स्थापना गरिएको छ । स्थानीयहरू त्यस ढुङ्गालाई भक्कु (आकाश भैरव) मानी पूजा गर्छन् । मन्दिरको दक्षिणमा एउटा धर्मधातुजिनालय चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको छ ।मन्दिरभित्र रहेको चैत्यलाई धनजु चैत्य किन भनियो भन्नेबारे स्थानीयले अनभिज्ञता प्रकट गरेका छन् । सम्भवतः इतुं बाहाः संघका धनजु नाम गरेका कुनै व्यक्तिले स्थापना गरेको हुनाले धनजु चैत्य भनिएको हुनुपर्छ । तर चैत्य र मन्दिरको स्थापनाबारे कुनै अभिलेख पाइएको छैन । मन्दिरको छानामुनि रहेको काष्ठकलाको आधारमा यस मन्दिरलाई ईशाको १० औं शताब्दीको मानिएको छ (Gutschow2011, p.218) । नेसं १०१४ (सन् १८९४) मा मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरी तोरण चढाइएको थियो । विसं १९९० (सन् १९३४) को भूकम्पभन्दा अघि यो मन्दिर दुई तलाको थियो र मन्दिरबाहिर प्रदक्षिणापथ बनाइएको थियो । भूकम्पले मन्दिर भत्केपछि पुनर्निर्माण गर्दा एक तलाको मात्र बनाइएको थियो र विसं २०४० (सन् १९८३) मा पहिलेको झिङ्गटीको छानाको ठाउँमा जस्तापाता राखिएको थियो (Gutschow2011, p.220)। मन्दिरको छानामुनि राखिएकोगःझ्याः(blind window) पहिले दोस्रो तलामा राखिएको हुनुपर्छ । मन्दिर पुनर्निर्माण गर्दा एक तले बनाइएपछि राख्ने ठाउँ नभएर छानामुनि राखिएको हुनुपर्छ । विसं २०७७ (सन् २०२१) मा काठमाडौं महानगरपालिकाको आर्थिक सहयोगमा मन्दिरको पुनर्निर्माण गरिएको थियो ।यस मन्दिरमा कायग ननिमा बस्ने एउटा वज्राचार्य परिवारले नित्यपूजा गरिरहेको छ । मन्दिरको उत्तरमा स्थापना गरिएको भक्कु (आकाश भैरव) को सम्बन्ध इन्द्रजात्रामा निकालिने सवःभक्कु नाचसित रहेको छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष हल्चोकका दुइँ (पुतुवार) हरू कायग ननिमा आउँछन् । कायग ननिभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने गल्लीमाथि रहेको घर[1]सवःभक्कु नाचसित सम्बन्धित मानिसहरूलाई बास बस्नको लागि बनाइएको हो । उनीहरू भाद्र शुक्ल १२ मा कायग ननिमा आउँछन् र भक्कु (आकाश भैरव) को विशेष पूजा गरी काठमाडौंका विभिन्न स्थानहरूमा आफ्नो नाच देखाउँछन् । आश्विन शुक्ल ३ मा पुनः भक्कु (आकाश भैरव) को समापन पूजा गरी घर फर्कन्छन् ।Footnotes^उक्त घर तण्डुकार थरको व्यक्तिको थियो । उनले घर शाक्य थरको व्यक्तिलाई बेचिसकेका छन् । तर इन्द्रजात्राको अवसरमा सवःभक्कु नाचलाई बास बस्न दिने शर्तमा घर बेचेका थिए ।

historical_events.event_name: Renovation of the caitya and offering a toraṇa
historical_events.event_description: The inscription on the fragment of atoraṇarecords a renovation of thecaityaand offering of thetoraṇa. The donors' names cannot be deciphered because the inscription has already decayed.
The Kathmandu Metropolitan City Office provided financial assistance for the reconstruction.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of dharmadhātujinālaya caitya (object number KAT1241-003)
historical_events.event_description: Thecaityaon the monument's southern side was built by Divyaratna, Hīrāmāyā, Prakāśaratna, Karuṇā and other family members.
